wave: TRUST BOUNDARY -- a declared root that is itself a symlink can escape the repository boundary
wave_title: adapter::source::inventory_from_roots decided whether to walk each root (both the single inventory_source root and each inventory_declared_source manifest-declared root) via Path::is_dir()/Path::is_file(), both of which follow symlinks. A declared root that is itself, on disk, a symlink to outside the repository (e.g. source_roots = ["vendor"] where vendor -> /etc) was silently followed and fully walked, reading real file content from outside the intended boundary -- a second, distinct escape vector from the `..`/absolute-path string escape fixed two generations ago, which declared_root_is_contained's lexical check cannot see at all (the string "vendor" is perfectly ordinary; only the filesystem knows it is a symlink).

generation_model.G_n: 478707ebe7 (docs(evidence): investigate normalization/census/extractor sweep, defer one finding) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct adversarial self-testing of this session's own prior security fix, per the standing loop's own instruction to generate scenarios that specifically exploit a capability once a generation gains it. Having fixed the string-level `..`/absolute-path escape (66b796d7de) and the allowed_paths defense-in-depth follow-on (aba88aa752), asked: what OTHER way could a declared root escape the repository that a purely lexical string check cannot see? Symlinks were the obvious next angle -- confirmed by tracing `inventory_from_roots`'s use of `Path::is_dir()`/`is_file()` (which follow symlinks) versus `visit_inventory`'s own nested-walk use of `DirEntry::file_type()` (which correctly does not). Proved the vulnerability was real BEFORE fixing it: wrote the regression test first (`a_declared_root_that_is_itself_a_symlink_escaping_the_repository_is_never_followed`), ran it against the unfixed code, and confirmed it failed with a real leaked artifact (`vendor/secret.rs`, real file content, from a real sibling directory outside the declared root) -- falsification-first, not merely inferred from reading the code.

priority_classification: security/trust boundary (priority 2) -- the same class and severity as the `..`/absolute-path escape fixed earlier this session, reachable through the exact same untrusted input surface (`.atlas/repo.toml` manifest arrays, not necessarily pre-admitted trusted config per `EXTERNAL-PROVIDER-TRUST.md`'s own candidate-reconciliation and donor-corpus-sweep scenarios).

design_decisions.question: Fix by extending `declared_root_is_contained` (the lexical string check), or at the filesystem-access point?
design_decisions.decision: At the filesystem-access point (`inventory_from_roots`), not the lexical check. `declared_root_is_contained` operates on the manifest string alone, before any filesystem access -- it fundamentally cannot know whether a given name resolves to a symlink on disk, and trying to make it aware of the filesystem would blur the layering this session has otherwise kept clean (a pure, testable-without-a-filesystem lexical predicate vs. the actual filesystem-walk sink). The correct fix is exactly the same shape as `visit_inventory`'s own existing, already-correct symlink handling: check `fs::symlink_metadata` (never follows the final component) before deciding how to treat a path, and this needed to happen at `inventory_from_roots`'s own top-level loop, the one place that was inconsistent with the rest of the walker.

design_decisions.question: Does this affect `inventory_source`'s own single root (the plain, non-manifest fallback)?
design_decisions.decision: No functional change for the normal case: `inventory_source` calls `root.as_ref().canonicalize()?` before ever reaching `inventory_from_roots`, and `canonicalize()` fully resolves symlinks -- the canonicalized `root` passed in can never itself be a symlink by the time this new check runs. The new check is a no-op for that path and only changes behavior for `inventory_declared_source`'s manifest-declared roots, which are joined (`root.join(path)`) without canonicalizing each individual declared root.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A declared root that is itself a symlink to outside the repository is never walked, recorded instead as an IgnoredByExplicitPolicy-equivalent Symlink artifact (matching the existing nested-symlink handling); an ordinary declared root (file, directory, or nonexistent) is walked exactly as before, with zero behavioral change.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: New test `a_declared_root_that_is_itself_a_symlink_escaping_the_repository_is_never_followed`: creates a real symlink on disk pointing to a real sibling directory containing a real file, declares it as a source root, and asserts the resulting inventory contains zero artifacts referencing that file. Written and run against the UNFIXED code first, confirmed to fail with the real leaked artifact path (`vendor/secret.rs`), then confirmed to pass after the fix -- proof the test exercises the real vulnerability, not a hypothetical one. All 3 pre-existing declared-root tests (escaping-via-dotdot, absolute-path, ordinary-root) re-run unchanged.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Re-ran `atlas-cli systemize --root .` against this repository's own real `.atlas/repo.toml`: `coding_admission` unchanged (still only the pre-existing `ADL_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED`/WebUI gap), `inventory` still closed -- this repository's own real manifest declares no symlinked roots, so the fix produces zero regression on its own real state.

implementation.sink_enforcement: adapter/src/source/mod.rs -- inventory_from_roots now checks fs::symlink_metadata(&path) before Path::is_dir()/is_file(); a symlinked root is recorded via the existing classify_non_file(..., ArtifactKind::Symlink, "symlink-not-followed") path instead of being walked

the three pre-existing declared-root tests (dotdot escape, absolute path, ordinary root) re-run unchanged -- confirms no regression to the string-level defenses or normal walking behavior
real self-census of this repository's own real manifest -- zero regression, no symlinked roots present

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. Closes a second, distinct path-escape vector found by directly adversarially testing this session's own prior security fix: a manifest-declared root that is itself a symlink to outside the repository is now refused the same way nested symlinks already were, rather than being silently followed and fully walked. Proven real via falsification-first testing (the exploit test failed against unfixed code with real leaked content before it was fixed).
